One model: a control does an action

Every on-screen control and every controller button does one thing: a controller button or stick, a key (with Shift, Ctrl or Alt), a mouse button, mouse movement or the wheel, or a Playport action (menu, keyboard, gyro on/off). Layouts are saved per game. Gamepad, Keyboard & mouse and Point & click are where you start; editing one makes it the game's own.

Auto means no surprises

On-screen controls show only while no controller is connected and hide the moment one connects. Playport suggests a layout from what the game reads (XInput or only keyboard and mouse); the person's choice wins. Without a controller, the Playport button at the top opens the in-game menu that the Home button opens.

Gyro aims like a mouse

Gyro moves the mouse 1:1 (no acceleration, no dead zone), or the right stick for a game that reads only a controller. It comes from the controller's gyro when it has one, else the iPhone's. It calibrates itself whenever the device is still, and Player space turning works however the phone is held. When it is on, it just works: no button to hold. A pause button (none by default) can be set to recentre.

Edit where you play

The editor opens over the paused game, so controls go where the game's own HUD is not. 8 pt grid, snapping to other controls, pinch to resize, undo. Each control: what it presses, label, size, hold/toggle/repeat. Sticks start where the thumb lands; a double tap on a stick is L3/R3.

Feel

Glass controls over the game; amber while held, with a light haptic tick. Several fingers at once. Every held control, key and button is let go when the menu opens, the app leaves the front or the layout changes, so nothing stays stuck.

A controller in a keyboard-only game

Game options › Controller: As a controller (XInput, today's behaviour), As keyboard & mouse (a ready map: left stick WASD, right stick mouse look, triggers mouse buttons), or Custom. Press the controller's button to pick it, then choose what it presses. Home stays Playport's.
